newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks break 1400 resistance, climb 2.98pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks break 1400 resistance, climb 2.98pct.

text.p: Tuesday was another strong day for the Greek bourse as the index settled 2.98 percent higher on very heavy volume with market watchers saying the rise would be sustained because of increased cash inflows.

"The interest rate cuts is what drove people to the market. With every passing day, more and more people invest in equities and this inflow of capital keeps the index climbing," said Yianna Tziovara, assistant portfolio manager at Allianz Mutual Fund.
Retail investors, are becoming more trusting towards the bourse as they witness its constant rise and opportunities for capital gains, she said.

"Therefore this rally is self-supported, mainly by domestic demand for stocks and aside from good market fundamentals more money keeps coming in as people are psychologically swept into the market," she added, expecting the next resistance level at 1,500 points.
Meanwhile, the Greek bourse was the second best performing emerging market, according to IFC investable indices, with a year-to-date $ return of 37 percent.
The news was expected to attract more foreign investors to Greek equities.
Commercial Securities, in its daily report, estimated the next resistance level at 1,700 points, after the market tests the 1,380-1,450 range.
"This would be the last testing area before 1,700 points," the report said.
The Athens general share index ended 2.98 percent or 40.73 points higher at 1407.65 points from Monday's 1366.92, after opening at 1370.06. The session's high was at 1413.13 points.
Turnover was 32.8 billion drachmas on volume of 9.4 million shares. Advancers led decliners 180 to 60 with 23 issues unchanged on 263 traded.
Investment shares led the rally with a strong rise of 6.27 percent, while construction shares followed with an increase of 5.54 percent.
Banks rose 5.06 percent and small caps gained 2.24 percent.
